guarantees.claim: Static lint assertion requires SecStartTriggerDelay == 0, reporting an error if non-zero.
Inside gen_start_delay (SecStartTriggerDelay > 0), count_d is assigned: if (!start_i) then '0; else if start_trigger then count_q; else count_q + 1'b1.
Inside gen_start_delay, start_trigger is asserted when count_q equals SecStartTriggerDelay[WidthCounter-1:0].
mux_sel_err is the bitwise OR of mux_sel_err_i and mr_err.

assumptions.claim: count_q is a sequential flop that updates from count_d each cycle, providing a stable counter state.
assumptions.risk: start_trigger generation may be corrupt or count_d ignored, leading to stuck or erratic start behavior.

assumptions.claim: start_i is deasserted to reset count_d to zero; the logic relies on start_i going low after a trigger to reset the counter.
assumptions.risk: if start_i remains high indefinitely, count_d will not reset and start_trigger may stay asserted, causing spurious or stuck AES start.

uncertain_points.claim: The static lint assertion (SecStartTriggerDelay == 0) contradicts the generate block that implements a start delay when SecStartTriggerDelay > 0. It is unclear whether the parameter is intended to be zero only, or if the assertion is stale/overridable.
uncertain_points.cond: when SecStartTriggerDelay is set to a non-zero value
uncertain_points.risk: If the assertion is bypassed or the parameter is changed, unintended start delay could violate SCA measurement timing or system startup protocols, causing functional failure.

uncertain_points.claim: Counter state count_q is used in start_trigger generation, but its reset or initialization is not visible in this chunk. An unknown initial value could cause a false start_trigger.
uncertain_points.cond: when system powers up or comes out of reset and SecStartTriggerDelay > 0
uncertain_points.risk: An unintended start_trigger pulse could prematurely start an AES key expansion or cipher operation.
